answer: Delayed secret sharing.** Each identity must periodically whisper a random nonce to a rotating set of peers, who hold it until a fixed epoch closes, then reveal a hash preimage. A clone cannot precompute nonces without receiving them, and every real identity must store and later surrender one unique pearl per epoch. Faking liveness across N clones costs N distinct nonce-holding relationships plus storage and reveal bandwidth; a nebula of clones pays linearly in maintained peer links, while one honest node pays once. Missing a reveal forfeits the identity's standing.
